concepts.def: Number showing change vs a base year (=100).
Wage in current pounds, not inflation-adjusted.
Retail Price Index — older UK inflation measure.
Importance given to each item in the basket.

walkthroughs.body_html: Base year 2015 = 100. By 2024 CPI = 130. Prices have risen 30% since 2015. From 2023 (CPI 124) to 2024 (CPI 130), annual inflation = (130 − 124) / 124 × 100 ≈ 4.8%.
Nominal wage rose 3%, inflation was 5%. Real wage change ≈ 3 − 5 = −2%. Workers feel poorer despite a 'pay rise'. That's the cost of inflation for fixed-income groups. Always check real, not nominal.
Housing is ~30% of household spending, so it has a big weight in CPI. A 10% rise in rent moves CPI more than a 10% rise in chewing gum. Weights are updated annually to reflect changing habits.
